title: Seeing a Healthcare Provider
goal: Report symptoms and concerns accurately, ask about an examination or care plan, and check the next step.

runs.text: A useful report explains
where
when it started
what it feels like
, and
whether it changes
. You can use short sentences. Not knowing the cause is different from not knowing what you experience.

study.title: Give a report and answer follow-up questions

turns.speaker: Patient

runs.text: I've had a cough for a week, and it's getting worse.

turns.en: I've had a cough for a week, and it's getting worse.

turns.speaker: Clinician

runs.text: Have you noticed any other symptoms?

turns.en: Have you noticed any other symptoms?

turns.speaker: Patient

runs.text: I've also felt tired. I don't know whether I've had a fever.

turns.en: I've also felt tired. I don't know whether I've had a fever.

blocks.caption: Give a report and answer follow-up questions · Patient & Clinician

runs.text: “Since Monday” names a starting point; “for a week” names a duration. “It comes and goes” means it is not constant. “It hurts when I move my arm” connects pain with an action. “It's getting better / worse” describes a change.
More specific reports: “I've been throwing up since last night.” “My shoulder hurts when I lift it.” “My child has a fever.” “I found a lump in my breast.”
Lump
means a raised or solid area you noticed; this report does not decide its cause.
Under the weather
is a broad conversational phrase for feeling unwell. For a clinical question, add concrete symptoms rather than relying on the idiom alone.

turns.speaker: Clinician

runs.text: I'd like to check your temperature and examine your shoulder.

turns.en: I'd like to check your temperature and examine your shoulder.

turns.speaker: Patient

runs.text: Please tell me before you touch the painful area.

turns.en: Please tell me before you touch the painful area.

turns.speaker: Clinician

runs.text: Of course. Let me know what you feel.

turns.en: Of course. Let me know what you feel.

turns.speaker: Patient

runs.text: I will. Could I have an interpreter for the explanation afterward?

turns.en: I will. Could I have an interpreter for the explanation afterward?

blocks.caption: Discuss examination and care · Clinician & Patient

runs.text: A
checkup
is a health assessment. A
shot / injection
introduces a substance using a needle.
Referral
means directing you to another professional or service.
Tests
investigate a question; being referred for a test does not, by itself, name a diagnosis.
You may hear “I'd like to change the dressing” or “I'd like to order a blood test.” A
dressing
covers a wound. Ask what the proposed procedure involves rather than guessing.

turns.speaker: Patient

runs.text: What do you think is causing this?

turns.en: What do you think is causing this?

turns.speaker: Clinician

runs.text: We need to discuss what we know and what we still need to check.

turns.en: We need to discuss what we know and what we still need to check.

turns.speaker: Patient

runs.text: What are the next steps? Are there other options?

turns.en: What are the next steps? Are there other options?

turns.speaker: Clinician

runs.text: I'll explain the plan and give you written information.

turns.en: I'll explain the plan and give you written information.

turns.speaker: Patient

runs.text: How will I get any test results, and who should I contact if things change?

turns.en: How will I get any test results, and who should I contact if things change?

blocks.caption: Understand the explanation and follow-up · Patient & Clinician

runs.text: Questions about antibiotics, rest, food, fluids, or other care need answers for your situation. This chapter does not supply a diagnosis or a treatment recipe. “Do I need antibiotics?” is a question, not an assumption that they are needed.

For a repeat prescription: “I'm running low on my regular medicine. Can we discuss the refill?” For a flu vaccination: “I'd like to ask about getting a flu shot.” These are requests to discuss care, not eligibility claims.

turns.speaker: Patient

runs.text: I want to make sure I understood. You want me to arrange the test, then contact this office for the results—is that right?

turns.en: I want to make sure I understood. You want me to arrange the test, then contact this office for the results—is that right?

turns.speaker: Clinician

runs.text: Let me clarify the sequence for your plan.

turns.en: Let me clarify the sequence for your plan.

turns.speaker: Patient

runs.text: Please write down who I should contact and when.

turns.en: Please write down who I should contact and when.

blocks.caption: Confirm without pretending to understand · Patient & Clinician

runs.text: You can be direct: “I don't understand that term.” “I still have a question.” You do not have to say everything is clear to end the visit politely.
Fictional report: shoulder pain since Monday, worse when lifting the arm, cause unknown, medicine list available. No treatment or results plan has been selected.
Give the report. Partner asks where, when, and what changes the pain. Answer without inventing a diagnosis.
Partner proposes an examination. Ask what it involves and request that they tell you before touching the sore area.
Partner says a test may be needed. Ask why, how results will be communicated, and who to contact if the situation changes.
Try another role: a breast lump noticed yesterday. State the observation without naming its cause.
Solo: read the clinician's prompts and speak your patient turns; then summarize your main concern without the role card. Change one timing or symptom detail later.
Possibilities:

“Since Monday, especially when I lift my arm.” “What are you checking with that test?” “I noticed a lump yesterday and want to have it assessed.” Check that the symptom, uncertainty, question, and unresolved next step remain clear.
Source note: Reporting and clarification principles informed by [NIH communication guidance](https://medlineplus.gov/talkingwithyourdoctor.html); all patients and exchanges are invented.

ja: 症状を伝え、説明を確認する。
note: 症状がいつからか、どう変わったかを話します。診察の説明や次の手順は、自分の言葉で確認できます。
